newsitem.title: CHINA: EB Int'l mulls Shanghai property stake.
newsitem.headline: EB Int'l mulls Shanghai property stake.

text.p: China Everbright International Ltd said on Friday it was in talks to acquire a stake in a major property development in Shanghai.
The project, Kerry Everbright City in the Zhabei district of the Chinese city, was valued at HK$2.68 billion as at May 31, 1996, according to the listing prospectus of Kerry Properties Ltd.
At that valuation, a 25 percent stake would cost HK$670 million.
Kerry Properties holds 54.45 percent of the project.

China Everbright International would acquire the stake from parent China Everbright Holdings Company Ltd (CEH) by taking a 25 percent interest in the issued share capital of Hong Kong Shanghai Development Co Ltd, the company said in an announcement released through the Hong Kong stock exchange.
Hong Kong Shanghai Development is involved in the development of Kerry Everbright City, the statement said.
Discussions were still at a preliminary stage, it said.
Kerry Everbright City is a multi-use development which sits on a total land area of 64,274 square metres (691,845 square feet), according to Kerry Properties' listing prospectus.
The property was to be developed into a commercial and residential complex in several phases, the prospectus said.
Phase I was to comprise a 33-storey office tower, a 34-storey office/residential tower on a four-storey commercial podium plus two basement levels, it said.
The entire complex was originally designed to be developed into 1.55 million sq ft of office, retail and residential space with parking facilities.
Only Phase I is under development.
The commercial podium was completed last September. At the end of 1996, 77 percent of the floor area of the section was leased and generating profit, Kerry Properities said in its 1996 annual report.
China Everbright International shares ended HK$0.65 higher at HK$4.90 on Friday.
